## TQQQ Read
- Momentum: **Neutral** (RSI 43.5, between 30 and 70). It climbed from 33.3 and is off the near-oversold zone. For a put seller, the oversold-and-stabilizing setup that brings richer premium has mostly passed. The bounce was fast, and premium is cheap against realized movement (see below).
- Market structure: **SIDEWAYS**. Spot is 18.6% under the $74.24 4-week high, short of the 20% line. VXN is 26.74, past the 25 line, so only the volatility leg of DOWNTURN is met. Spot is 20.3% above the 4-week low, short of the 30% line for RALLY, which would need a close above about $65.33 (1.3 × $50.25), 8.1% above spot. A close under about $59.39 (0.8 × $74.24), 1.7% below spot, would put DOWNTURN back in place. The label is fragile in both directions.
- Trend: below the 50DMA by 15.35% and below the 200DMA by 7.7%. Spot is 31.10% under the 52-week high and 62.6% above the 52-week low ($60.44 / $37.16).
- Volatility & premium environment: VXN is 26.74, down 6.41% on the day. The chain's ATM IV is 0.66, and IV/HV is 0.65 (HV20 106.6%). IV/HV under 1 means options cost less than the stock has actually been moving, so sellers get no extra cushion. Premium is large in dollars, but swings are large too. The chain IV of 66% is about 18% under the ~80% implied by the 3x-VXN rule of thumb, which is itself only an estimate.
- Put-selling context: HOSTILE. The stage is 5, six of seven lenses are bearish, credit is still over its lines, spot is under both moving averages, and the news engine flags SHOCK. IV/HV of 0.65 means premium is cheap relative to realized movement. A one-day +6.86% bounce with VIX under 20 makes this label more fragile than last read. A close above the 200DMA near $65.48 together with credit back under its lines would be the first real softening. Context only — no strikes, expiries or sizes.
